# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 18

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 35

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "had a very great light" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "had a blazing abundance of light" (PNEUMA — expands). EMET/LOGOS preferred.

**v. 1** — "heard their voice but did not see their form" — all three agree on substance; no structural dispute.

**v. 2** — "treated unjustly, did not harm them" (EMET) vs. "wronged without being harmed in return" (LOGOS) vs. "wronged and had not struck back" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 2** — "begged pardon for the fact that they had been at variance" (EMET) vs. "begged pardon for having been at odds" (LOGOS) vs. "begged forgiveness for the enmity that had existed" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "glorious exile" (EMET) vs. "glorious exodus" (LOGOS) vs. "glorious march into freedom" (PNEUMA — expands). LOGOS preferred: "exodus" more contextually appropriate than EMET's "exile."

**v. 4** — "imprisoned your sons" (EMET) vs. "kept your sons confined" (LOGOS) vs. "locked away your sons" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "the imperishable light of the law was going to be given to the age" (EMET) vs. "the imperishable light of the law was to be given to the world" (LOGOS) vs. "the undying light of the law was meant to be given to the world" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "planned to kill the infants of the holy ones" (EMET) vs. "devised a plan to kill the infants of the holy ones" (LOGOS) vs. "plotted to murder the Hebrew infants" (PNEUMA — adds "Hebrew," not in text). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "one child had been exposed and saved" (EMET) vs. "one child was exposed and rescued" (LOGOS) vs. "one child was exposed and rescued" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "removed a multitude of their sons" (EMET) vs. "took away a multitude of their children" (LOGOS) vs. "took away a vast number of their children" (PNEUMA — adds "vast"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 5** — "mighty torrent" (EMET) vs. "mighty flood" (LOGOS) vs. "mighty flood" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 6** — "knowing with certainty what oaths they had trusted" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "knowing clearly what promises they had trusted" (PNEUMA). EMET/LOGOS preferred; "oaths" is the more precise translation of ὅρκων.

**v. 8** — "glorified us when you summoned us" (EMET) vs. "glorified us whom you had called" (LOGOS) vs. "raised us up with glory when you called us out" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "put into effect with one accord the divine law" (EMET) vs. "put into effect with one accord the divine covenant" (LOGOS) vs. "sealed with one voice the divine covenant" (PNEUMA). Greek νόμον = law; LOGOS changes to "covenant" — interpretive but reasonable. SOPHIA: "covenant" (LOGOS), as the Passover is covenant-founding.

**v. 9** — "hymns of the fathers" (LOGOS) vs. "praises of the fathers" (EMET) vs. "praises of the fathers" (PNEUMA). Greek ᾠδάς = songs/hymns. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 10** — "discordant cry of the enemies rang back" (EMET) vs. "discordant cry of the enemies resounded back" (LOGOS) vs. "clashing dissonant cry of the enemies" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "commoner" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "commoner" (all agree). No dispute.

**v. 13** — "disbelieved everything on account of the enchantments" (EMET) vs. "skeptical of everything because of their sorceries" (LOGOS) vs. "sorceries had made them skeptical of everything" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — "the people was son of God" (EMET) vs. "this people was the son of God" (LOGOS) vs. "this people is the son of God" (PNEUMA — uses present tense). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 14** — "gentle silence held all things" (EMET) vs. "a gentle silence enveloped all things" (LOGOS) vs. "gentle silence — when all things lay wrapped in stillness" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 14** — "in the middle of its swift course" (EMET) vs. "at the midpoint of its swift course" (LOGOS) vs. "at the midpoint of its swift racing course" (PNEUMA — adds "racing"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 15** — "all-powerful word leaped from heaven" (EMET) vs. "all-powerful Word leaped down from heaven" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). Capitalization of "Word" — all three capitalize. LOGOS adopted.

**v. 15** — "stern warrior" (EMET) vs. "relentless warrior" (LOGOS) vs. "remorseless warrior" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 15** — "land of destruction" (EMET) vs. "land marked for destruction" (LOGOS) vs. "heart of a doomed land" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 16** — "bearing a sharp sword, your irrevocable decree" (EMET) vs. "bearing your sharp and irrevocable decree as a sword" (LOGOS) vs. "carrying your irrevocable sentence like a sharp sword" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 16** — "while it reached to heaven, it stood upon the earth" (EMET) vs. "while touching heaven, it stood upon the earth" (LOGOS) vs. "it touched the sky and stood upon the earth" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 17** — "apparitions in dreadful dreams" (EMET) vs. "visions in terrifying dreams" (LOGOS) vs. "nightmarish visions" (PNEUMA — condenses). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 21** — "propitiatory incense" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "incense that makes atonement" (PNEUMA). EMET/LOGOS preferred.

**v. 22** — "word he subdued the chastiser" (EMET) vs. "word he subdued the one who was inflicting punishment" (LOGOS) vs. "word that he mastered the one carrying out the punishment" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 23** — "fallen on one another in heaps" (EMET) vs. "falling on top of one another in heaps" (LOGOS) vs. "piling up, one upon another" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 23** — "cut off the way to the living" (EMET) vs. "cut off the path to the living" (LOGOS) vs. "cut off the road to the living" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 24** — "long robe" — all three agree. "Four rows of stones" (EMET) vs. "four rows of precious stones" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 24** — "crown upon his head" (EMET) vs. "diadem upon his head" (LOGOS) vs. "crown upon his head" (PNEUMA). Greek κίδαρις = the high priestly turban/headdress. LOGOS's "diadem" is more specific; adopted.

**v. 25** — "the destroyer gave way" (EMET) vs. "the Destroyer gave way" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). Capitalization: LOGOS/PNEUMA capitalize as a proper title, following the tradition of Exodus 12:23 and Hebrews 11:28. SOPHIA: "the Destroyer."

**v. 25** — "sufficient to test the wrath only by these" (EMET) vs. "it was enough to test the wrath with these alone" (LOGOS) vs. "enough simply to make trial of the wrath with these things alone" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.
